title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
abstract: arXiv:2608.25869v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assess generated content, giving rise to the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm. These systems now score outputs, filter content, and gate iterative refinement in production pipelines, where each judgment is often assumed to be independent of earlier evaluations. We test this assumption using three prompt conditions: no metadata, revision framing, and anchored metadata containing revision, attempt, and prior-score fields. We show that prior scores, even when included only as context metadata, anchor judgments and systematically shift ratings toward their values. Across 192,000 attempted evaluations (185,271 successful), seven out of the eight evaluated models have 95% task-stratified bootstrap intervals below zero for the total anchored-metadata effect on 20 fixed texts. Cohen's $d$, a standardized measure of the difference between score distributions, reaches an absolute value of 0.71. Token-level analysis

translated_title: 大语言模型作为评判系统中的锚定偏差：先验分数损害评估独立性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25869v1 公告类型：新公告 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地用于评估生成内容，催生了“LLM作为评判者”这一范式。这些系统现在在生产流程中对输出进行评分、过滤内容，并门控迭代细化，其中每个判断通常被假定独立于先前的评估。我们通过三种提示条件测试了这一假设：无元数据、修订框架以及包含修订、尝试和先验分数字段的锚定元数据。我们表明，即使仅作为上下文元数据包含，先验分数也会锚定判断，并系统地使评分向其值偏移。在192,000次尝试评估（185,271次成功）中，八个被评估模型中有七个对20个固定文本的总锚定元数据效应的95%任务分层自助法置信区间低于零。Cohen's d（评分分布差异的标准化度量）达到绝对值0.71。令牌级分析...
tldr: 本论文发现，在大语言模型评判系统中，即使先验分数仅作为上下文元数据提供，也会显著锚定后续评估，导致评分系统性偏移，破坏评估独立性。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that in LLM-as-a-Judge systems, even when prior scores are provided only as contextual metadata, they significantly anchor subsequent evaluations, causing systematic score shifts and compromising evaluation independence.
